books.title: Grundrisse
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Written in 1857-1858, the Grundrisse (German for 'Outlines') is a massive set of raw, private notebooks where Marx worked out his economic theories before writing Capital. Left unpublished until 1939, it contains Marx's most futuristic speculations on automation, technology, and the liberation of human free time.
books.subject: Theory & Philosophy

books.title: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written in Zurich in early 1916, during World War I, and first published as a pamphlet in mid-1917 in Petrograd. Lenin wrote it under tsarist censorship, forcing him to use cautious, 'Aesopian' language and focus on purely economic analysis. The work builds on J.A. Hobson's and Rudolf Hilferding's studies of imperialism and finance capital, synthesising their data into a Marxist framework that explains imperialism as a necessary stage of capitalist development, not merely a policy choice.
books.subject: Theory & Philosophy

books.title: The Communist Manifesto
books.author: Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Commissioned by the Communist League and published in London in February 1848, this pamphlet was written during a period of massive political unrest across Europe. It explains the class struggle and critiques capitalism, serving as a call to action for the working class.
books.subject: Theory & Philosophy

books.title: On Contradiction
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: A simplified guide to Mao Zedong's essay on how conflict and change work. It explains why opposing forces exist in everything and how focusing on the main problem helps solve real-life challenges.
books.subject: Dialectical Materialism & Philosophy

books.title: Value, Price and Profit
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: First published in 1865, this text forms an essential part of Karl Marx's critique of political economy. It provides simplified, yet rigorous, explanations of key capitalist economic concepts.
books.subject: Theory & Philosophy

books.title: Wage Labour and Capital
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Based on lectures Marx delivered in 1847 to the German Workingmen's Club in Brussels, this work provides a straightforward and accessible explanation of the economic relationships under capitalism, particularly how labor becomes a commodity and how wages are determined.
books.subject: Theory & Philosophy

books.title: What Is To Be Done?
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written by V.I. Lenin in late 1901 and published in 1902, this pivotal work argues for a disciplined, professional vanguard party to lead the working class beyond basic trade-union demands to full political consciousness.
